name: cw15 intracellular β-casein
description: Mixotrophic Chlamydomonas accumulating β-casein intracellularly, recovered by mild pulsed-electric-field disruption. The reference point sits where the literature actually is today — which is the bottom-left corner of this surface.

assumptions.label: Biomass density achieved (CC-137c, TAP)
assumptions.note: Wild-type C. reinhardtii in TAP reached 1.23 g/L in 96 h. The reference point assumes 2 g/L — already optimistic against this.

assumptions.label: Intracellular expression achieved (UVM4 reporters)
assumptions.note: UVM4/UVM11 reach ~0.2% TSP for intracellular reporters. No casein has been expressed in any alga, so the % TSP axis is entirely extrapolation beyond this point.

assumptions.label: PEF protein release, cell-wall-deficient
assumptions.note: Versus 11% for the walled wild type. The single strongest economic argument for cw15 as the chassis.

assumptions.label: Safe-harbor integration uplift
assumptions.note: LHCBM1 locus integration gave 8.6-fold higher accumulation than random insertion — the most actionable published route up the % TSP axis.

assumptions.label: Capital charge factor

basis.justification: Financial convention, not a measurement. The annualisation rate applied to CAPEX is a modelling choice the corpus has no opinion on.

assumptions.note: Annualisation rate. A modelling convention, not a measurement.

assumptions.label: Operating days per year

basis.justification: Plant availability assumption. A scheduling choice, not a property of the organism.

assumptions.note: Standard availability assumption for a continuous plant.

assumptions.label: CAPEX scaling exponent

basis.justification: The six-tenths rule, standard practice for capacity scaling. Convention, not literature.

assumptions.note: Six-tenths rule. Doubling capacity costs ~52% more, which is the main argument for building big.

assumptions.label: Photobioreactor reference capital

basis.justification: Reference capital for the sizing basis. A vendor-class figure the corpus holds no record for.

assumptions.note: Order-of-magnitude for a 120 m³ tubular installation, shaped by Acién’s real plant costs but not derived from them.

assumptions.label: TAP medium cost

basis.justification: Media cost basis, priced from components rather than measured. Ontology v1 has no field for a per-litre medium price.

assumptions.note: Includes acetate as the dominant carbon cost. Demo assumption — no citable price was retrieved.

assumptions.label: Batch duration

basis.justification: From the M6 cultivation description. Ontology v1 has no field for batch duration, so no record exists to bind — an ontology gap, not an unsourced number.

assumptions.note: Mixotrophic cultures reached maximum biomass in about 5 days.

assumptions.label: Real plant biomass cost, 3.8 t/y
assumptions.note: Two years of operating data from a real 30 m³ tubular plant. Currency deliberately not converted.

assumptions.label: Real plant biomass cost, scaled to 200 t/y
assumptions.note: The same plant simplified and scaled up — a 5.5× cost reduction from scale alone.

name: K. phaffii secreted comparator
description: The incumbent precision-fermentation route: a secreting yeast at fed-batch density. Anchored on the two real eukaryotic data points — Choi & Jiménez-Flores for bovine β-casein and Aro et al. for what secretion achieves at its best.

assumptions.label: β-lactoglobulin secreted titer (T. reesei)
assumptions.note: The current benchmark for a secreted milk protein. No casein has reached this in any host.

assumptions.label: β-casein intracellular (P. pastoris)
assumptions.note: Reported as 0.7–1.0 g/L at 15–18% TSP. Note this was intracellular: secretion with the native signal peptide reached only 0.005%.

assumptions.label: Secreted fraction, native signal peptide
assumptions.note: The warning that a native bovine signal peptide will not work in a non-mammalian eukaryote.

assumptions.label: Fed-batch cycle time

basis.justification: Process schedule for the comparator. A modelling choice, not a measured quantity.

assumptions.note: Typical methanol-induction fed-batch duration. Demo assumption.

assumptions.label: Defined medium cost

basis.justification: Media cost basis for the yeast comparator. Priced, not measured, and outside the ontology.

assumptions.note: Includes glycerol and methanol feed. Demo assumption.

assumptions.label: Media share of COGS (industry claim)
assumptions.note: Vendor and market sources put media at 35–50% of cost of goods. Non-peer-reviewed — excluded from aggregate statistics and never gold.

assumptions.label: Published-model average titer
assumptions.note: Across 55 published TEA models — an order of magnitude above anything achieved for casein.

assumptions.label: Private-benchmark average titer
assumptions.note: The gap between this and the published average is why GFI concludes published models systematically overstate cost.

assumptions.label: Capital charge factor

basis.justification: Financial convention, not a measurement. The annualisation rate applied to CAPEX is a modelling choice the corpus has no opinion on.

assumptions.note: Annualisation rate, same convention as S1 so the two are comparable.

assumptions.label: CAPEX scaling exponent

basis.justification: The six-tenths rule, standard practice for capacity scaling. Convention, not literature.

assumptions.note: Six-tenths rule.

name: Conventional β-casein from milk
description: The incumbent baseline. Cold microfiltration of micellar casein concentrate, exploiting β-casein’s dissociation from the micelle at low temperature. This is what any recombinant route has to beat.

assumptions.label: β-casein concentration in bovine milk
assumptions.note: The feedstock concentration that sets the whole cost structure — you process a litre to recover a couple of grams.

assumptions.label: Casein share of total milk protein
assumptions.note: Caseins are ~80% of bovine milk protein; β-casein is ~36% of the casein fraction.

assumptions.label: Isoelectric point
assumptions.note: Caseins precipitate readily at pI on acidification — the basis of the simplest isolation route.

assumptions.label: Cold microfiltration temperature

basis.justification: From the J3 process description. Ontology v1 has no field for a process temperature, so no record exists to bind — an ontology gap, not an unsourced number.

assumptions.note: β-casein dissociates from the micelle into the serum phase at ≤4 °C, which is what makes the separation possible.

assumptions.label: Raw milk price

basis.justification: Commodity price input. Market data rather than literature, and outside the ontology.

assumptions.note: Commodity price varies by region and season. Demo assumption — swept as a dimension because it dominates.

assumptions.label: Fractionation capital, annualised

basis.justification: Annualised capital for the incumbent train. A modelling choice on the sizing basis.

assumptions.note: Membrane plant capital per kg of β-casein. Demo assumption.

assumptions.label: Residual biomass co-product value
assumptions.note: Protein-rich residual streams are worth very little, which limits how much credit any process can claim for them.
